title: Compact funnel assessment + day-one activation
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, operational playbook for small-to-medium hiring funnels (IC and early manager hires). Designed for fast-moving teams where we want consistent signal from screen -> take-home -> panel and a repeatable Day-1 activation bundle. Keep short, actionable, and reusable by recruiting and hiring managers.

Scope
- Roles: IC (L3–L5), technical managers (first-level).
- Funnel stages covered: phone screen, technical take-home (optional), panel/onsite, debrief / decision.
- Post-offer: day-zero/day-one activation checklist and first 14-day learning cadence.

Quick notes (notes to self)
- Use this when reqs are <6 weeks. For long enterprise searches, expand into full scorecard.
- Keep take-home assignment <= 90 minutes. Too many take-homes = drop-off.
- Default to panel length 90 minutes (2 × 45 or 3 × 30).

Phone screen rubric (10–15 min)
- Goal: baseline technical competence, communication, and role interest.
- Use 5-question checklist: current stack, 1 quick system/problem question, code design sketch, culture fit, salary/constraints.
- Scoring: 0 = fail (no hire-signal), 1 = borderline, 2 = clear pass.
- Pass threshold -> invite take-home or panel (skip take-home for strong signal).

Sample phone probes
- "Walk me through a recent project where latency or cost mattered — what tradeoffs did you make?"
- "Given our inference use-case (low-latency text gen), how would you approach a perf regression?"
- Behavior: "Tell me about a time you pushed back on a roadmap decision and why."

Take-home (optional)
- Timebox: 60–90 minutes. Provide reproducible seed data and explicit acceptance criteria.
- Deliverable: short repo or gist + README with choices and tradeoffs. No need for production polish.
- Clear eval rubric: correctness (0–3), clarity of tradeoffs (0–3), simplicity/engineering judgment (0–3).

Panel / onsight rubric (45–90 min)
- Panel composition: 1 hiring mgr, 1 peer engineer, 1 cross-functional reviewer (SRE/infra or product depending on role).
- Structure: 10 min intro, 30–45 min technical, 10–15 min behavioral/collaboration, 5 min candidate Q&A.
- Scorecard categories (0–4 each): technical understanding, system design, coding/problem solving, communication, cross-team judgement.
- Decision rule: average score >= 3.0 and no single category <=1 -> strong hire. If avg 2.5–2.9 -> onsitelist/second loop. avg <2.5 -> decline.

Interview scoring guide (language for interviewers)
- 4 = exceptional: contributes new ideas, shows production ownership, articulates tradeoffs with examples.
- 3 = solid: correct approaches, good tradeoffs, production-aware.
- 2 = adequate: understands basic concepts, some gaps, would need ramp.
- 1 = weak: conceptual errors or missing fundamentals.
- 0 = fail: incorrect or unsafe recommendations.

Bias mitigation reminders
- Ask same core 3 prompts for each candidate in panel.
- Avoid hypothetical hypothetical chains — prefer concrete examples (STAR).
- Document unclear signal in comments, not in personal adjectives.

Decision debrief template (to paste into panel notes)
- Candidate: [name] | Role: [role] | Date: [date]
- Summary (2 sentences): technical strengths / risks
- Scores (list categories + numeric)
- Recommendation: HIRE / ONSLIST / NO
- Open concerns (blocking): [list]
- Proposed linkage to team ramp plan if hired: [mentor, first-3 projects]

Offer & preboarding quick checklist
- Recruiter: confirm comp band, manager approves, legal template -> offer email.
- HR: send background check invite (if applicable).
- Eng: create new calendar invite for intro + buddy pairing (Day 1 10:00AM).
- IT/SW: provision laptop image, VPN, SSO invite (ensure day-zero access to Slack and email).
- Security: add to access request queue (KMS read exempt until 30d unless approved).

Day-zero / Day-one activation (practical)
- Day-zero (before start): create accounts, email/SAML, Slack invite, give short welcome doc + org chart, onboarding calendar.
- Day-one morning: 09:00 welcome + HR quick talk (30m), 10:00 team intro + buddy pairing (30m), 11:00 engineering walkthrough (30m).
- Day-one afternoon: setup dev env checklist, first task assigned (tiny bug or doc update), sync with hiring manager 1:1 expectations (15m).

Day-one checklist (engineer-focused, quick)
- Confirm laptop received and encrypted.
- SSO/Slack/Google account active.
- Repo access granted (read).
- Dev env: can run unit tests locally (smoke).
- First task ticket created and assigned (label: day-1).
- Buddy assigned and first sync scheduled.

14-day ramp plan highlights
- Week 1: orientation, infra tour, local dev friction fixes, 1st code review.
- Week 2: small ownerable task, join on-call shadow (if relevant), first feedback loop.

Manager quick playbook for first 2 weeks
- Day 1–3: set 3 short-term outcomes (learning + impact), arrange meet-and-greets.
- Weekly 1:1 cadence for first month, 30m.
- End of week 2: 15m check-in with people-ops to confirm access and org fit.

Templates (snippets)
- Offer subject line: "Redwood Inference — Offer for [Role]"
- Short offer blurb (recruiters): "We were impressed by your experience with [X]. This note confirms our intent to offer [role] at [comp details]. Formal offer coming via DocuSign."

Open questions / follow-ups
- Align take-home policy across product vs infra teams (some teams reluctant).
- Audit panel representation for diverse interviewers. Add to next people-ops agenda.

Appendix: short evaluation worksheet (copy into panel doc)
- Candidate: [name]
- Role fit quick bullets
- Numeric scores (phone, take-home, panel) -> final decision field
- Debrief notes and action items

References / links
- Confluence compact funnel page (linked above)
- Slack: #people-ops (use for quick flagging of candidate scheduling / escalations)

Endnotes
- Keep file minimal. Use this doc as the canonical short-play and fork into role-specific scorecards when needed.
- If we repeatedly see <50% pass rate at phone->panel, revisit the job description and recruiter brief.
